events.title: Patch CL6750 - Ultrawide, ultra-tidy.
events.summary: ### Full game and demo - There's a new HUD aspect ratio setting under Display (Full, 21:9 or 16:9). events.title: Patch CL6683 - Time to head down for après.
events.summary: - Closing time works like a real mountain now. When a lift closes, its line gets roped off, but anyone already waiting still gets their ride. Nobody new joins. - Guests heading home after close can always ski down, even on runs without night skiing. They'll take a lit run when there is one, and after dark they'd rather ride a running lift down than feel their way down an unlit trail. - Guests on their way home walk down snowy trails instead of getting stuck at the top. - Fixed guests sometimes t

events.title: Patch CL6582 - Small fixes, smoother controls
events.summary: - Scenarios can be picked with a controller now. The D-pad moves through the list and A starts the one you've chosen. - The snowblower's coverage marks only show up while you're placing a snowblower, not every time you place a building. - The Patch Notes window is easier to read, with more room between bullets, larger text, and older releases folded away until you open them.

events.title: Nobody lives at the top of the lift anymore
events.summary: Guests who ride to the top of a lift are offered every run that actually starts up there, with no hidden distance limit on which ones count. A summit's worth of riders could end up with nowhere to go and quietly give up on the day. A lift whose top station has no run beginning inside it now stops and says so. A trail you can't drop into reads "No way in" and names the hub to drag its start inside of. Guests who already gave up get a second chance. Fix the layout and they pick themselves back up

events.title: Fixes for lift lines, drop-offs, and guests who can't commit
events.summary: Fixed guests freezing at the top of a lift. They'd start down one run, decide the neighboring one looked better, turn back, and do it again until closing. Riders get off the lift at the lift, not twenty meters out in the flats. A few unlucky ones were being set down where there's nothing to ski to, and they'd stand there until they gave up on the day. Lift lines move again. Guests mid-line no longer settle in place well short of their spot, and whoever's at the front actually gets a chair instea

events.title: Guests have stopped teleporting into the bar
events.summary: Lift lines work like real lines. There's one place to walk up, you join at the back, and nobody walks through the person in front of them to get there. Guests stop lining up for a lift once it's finished running for the day. They used to collect at a dead lift after close, get shooed off, and wander right back. A guest who can't actually walk to a lodge or a bar now picks somewhere else. Before, some of them would give up on the walk and turn up inside the building anyway. Fixed guests getting s

events.title: Everyone was squeezing into the bowl through the same door
events.summary: Guests find their own way into a bowl instead of funneling through one spot on the rim. They pick a fresh line each lap, so a crowd spreads across the face rather than wearing a single rut into it. Skiers who slipped out the side of a bowl used to end up parked in a far corner of the map for the rest of the day. A bowl run ends at the rim now, and anyone who drifts off it gets collected instead of setting off for the horizon. Guests no longer pace back and forth at a lift line without ever joini

events.title: Turns out the lift line rope was there for a reason
events.summary: Guests walk around a lift line's rope instead of straight through the middle of it. It showed up most often right after you dropped a new building next to a lift. A fence is just a fence again. Drawing one no longer invents a named area of its own out in the middle of nowhere, and it won't stretch one across ground nobody can walk. events.title: The guests have opinions now, and one of them wants a spa
events.summary: This one covers three builds' worth of work, so settle in. Blueprints Reputation no longer hands you buildings and lifts outright. Reaching a tier opens up its blueprints, you buy each one once, and after that you pay the usual build cost every time you place it. The build menu is the blueprint browser now.
